claimsToVerify: Romans cleaned skin primarily by applying oil and scraping it away with a bronze or iron strigil rather than soap.
The standard circuit included the caldarium (hot room), tepidarium (warm room), and frigidarium (cold plunge).
Roman thermal complexes functioned as multi-purpose civic hubs featuring food vendors, exercise yards (palaestrae), and social networking.
